summary: Round 4 tested end-to-end after MongoDB→MariaDB migration and 2 new features (Trusted Driver Badge + Admin Driver Payouts). Backend: dedicated Round-4 suite (/app/backend/tests/test_round4_payouts_trusted.py) — 12/12 pass. Full suite serially: 54/55 pass (1 pre-existing failure unrelated to Round 4: TestOrderFlow.test_preset_order_flow expects service_fee=35.0 but backend now returns 44.0 because the preset store's total weight is now factored in via dynamic pabili fee — this is a stale round-1 assertion, not a bug). MariaDB compatibility layer (db_mysql.py) works transparently: signup email+pw, signup phone+name, login both ways, /auth/me, full ride lifecycle w/ fare & eta_minutes, full pabili lifecycle w/ dynamic service_fee & eta_minutes, python-computed rating rollup (rating_count/rating_avg update on /auth/me after POST /ratings) all verified. NEW /api/admin/payouts: admin-only (403 for driver & customer, 401 no-token); shape {from,to,report[],totals{drivers,rides,orders,ride_earnings,pabili_earnings,total}}; report sorted desc by total; date_from=2099 returns empty; today-range totals sum matches row sums. NEW config keys trusted_min_ratings & trusted_min_avg surface on GET /api/config (public) and update via POST /api/admin/config. Frontend: Admin Overview shows the 'Driver Payouts' card → Payouts screen renders presets (All time / Today / Last 7 days / This month), summary card (verified ₱917 total, 3 drivers, 13 rides, 4 pabili, ride fares ₱745, pabili fees ₱172), per-driver rows (Mang Tonyo ₱721 / Dihon Dihon ₱147 / Applicant One ₱49), and 'Today' preset filters correctly to 1 row. 'Export as CSV' on web shows the expected 'CSV export works on the mobile app' toast (native path uses expo-file-system/legacy + expo-sharing — not exercised on web, per instruction). Admin Pricing tab now has a 'Trusted Driver Badge' section with testIDs config-trusted_min_ratings and config-trusted_min_avg; Save persists (toast 'Pricing updated' confirmed). After lowering thresholds to (1, 4), Trusted badge appears on admin drivers-list rows for qualifying drivers (verified on Applicant One 4.0★/1 rating) and on the driver Earnings rating card (5.0/5.0 · Trusted visible). Trusted badge also wired to tracking screen driver card (code verified: /app/frontend/app/track/[kind]/[id].tsx:199-200).

react_native_issues.issue: React Native Web deprecation warning persists: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' Cosmetic only. Reference: /app/frontend/src/theme.ts SHADOW.card.
React Native Web deprecation warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Cosmetic; migrate JSX prop into style.

action_items: (Optional) Update /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py::TestOrderFlow::test_preset_order_flow — its hardcoded assert order['service_fee'] == 35.0 is stale after Round 3 dynamic pabili fee (weight-based). Preserve seed store weights or relax the assertion to service_fee >= 35.

(Optional) db_mysql.py update_one/update_many/delete/find_one_and_update do a full-table load per call (SELECT * then filter in Python). Fine for MVP volume (<10k docs) but plan an index/where-clause path for high-cardinality collections (rides, orders) as data grows.
(Optional polish) Migrate SHADOW.* to boxShadow and JSX pointerEvents into style={{ pointerEvents: ... }} to silence RN Web deprecation warnings.

(Optional) parallel xdist run of the full backend suite still produces `Email already registered` on module fixtures whenever a preview backend reload happens between the two worker imports (auto-reload can duplicate the signup). Serial (-n 0) is clean. Consider setting reload=False in supervisor for backend or making signup idempotent for TEST_ emails.
critical_code_review_comments: db_mysql.py `_matches` `$exists` uses `value is not _MISSING` — correct since missing keys return the _MISSING sentinel (line 113). Also correctly treats explicit None value as 'exists' which matches Mongo behavior.
db_mysql.py `update_one(..., upsert=True)` synthesizes `id` if not provided (line 289-291). Good — matches call-site expectations for config upsert keyed by id='pricing'.
db_mysql.py `find_one` has a fast-path for pk lookups (`id` only) but `update_one`/`delete_one` always do a full table load. Acceptable for MVP volume but flagged in action_items.

server.py admin_payouts (lines 746-803) correctly filters by `updated_at[:10]` for the date window and gates behind require_role('admin'). Returns sensible empty structure for out-of-range dates. Totals recomputed from rows so they always sum consistently. Good.
server.py rating flow now computes rating_avg/rating_count in Python (per problem statement), verified via test that /auth/me reflects the new count/avg after POST /ratings.
server.py is 1171 lines (was 1112 in R3) — still past 700-line guideline. Splitting into routers (auth, rides, orders, admin, driver, config) will make Round-5 changes safer.
frontend payouts.tsx correctly gates native-only export behind Platform.OS !== 'web' and shows an informative toast on web (line 81-84). CSV builds proper header + totals row.

frontend config.tsx: the Trusted section is validated together with the numeric fields (line 96-101). Note: trusted_min_ratings should logically be an integer — the UI accepts decimals via keyboardType='decimal-pad'. Backend currently accepts float and it works, but consider Math.floor on save or a separate keyboardType='number-pad' for ratings.
TrustedBadge component (29 lines) is a small, isolated, testID-friendly presentational component. Good.
isTrusted() in theme.ts uses default fallbacks (3, 4.5) if cfg is not loaded yet — prevents flicker/undefined-check errors at first render.

success_rate.backend: 100% for Round-4 (12/12); 98.2% overall serial (54/55, 1 pre-existing R1 preset-fee assertion is stale)
success_rate.frontend: 100% for the 3 Round-4 features tested (payouts card+screen+presets+summary+rows+export web toast; trusted-badge config section save+persist; trusted badge visibility on admin drivers list + driver earnings screen)
